items.title: Determination of a Vector from its Rectangular Components

source_refs.note: Determination of a Vector from its Rectangular Components: a main subheading of 2.2 Vectors, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 23-25.

blocks.text: If the rectangular components of a vector as shown in Fig.(2.1) are given, we can find out the magnitude of the vector by using Pythagorean Theorem.

blocks.title: Example 2.1
blocks.problem: Find the angle between two forces of equal magnitude when the magnitude of their resultant is also equal to the magnitude of either of these forces.
steps: Let θ be the angle between two forces F₁ and F₂, where F₁ is along x-axis. Then

x-component of their resultant will be:
Rx = F₁ cos 0° + F₂ cos θ
Rx = F₁ + F₂ cos θ

And y-component of their resultant is
Ry = F₁ sin 0° + F₂ sin θ
Ry = F₂ sin θ
The resultant R is given by R² = Rx² + Ry²

Hence F² = (F + F cos θ)² + (F sin θ)²
F² = F² + F²cos²θ + 2F² cos θ + F² sin²θ
